gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-002 explicitly identifies the same reciprocal obstacle profile V=1/f, notes its non-integrable singularity on and inside the obstacle, and concludes that the functional is not well defined. This is the same failure of the proposed V to satisfy the regularity and integrability requirements needed for the full-domain variational construction.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The reciprocal obstacle potential has a denominator vanishing on the obstacle surface, so it is singular rather than a legitimate smooth/C2, integrable input to the stated functional and gradient-based calculation.

component_coverage.gold_component: The proposed reciprocal obstacle profile is singular at the zero set of its denominator and therefore is not a valid smooth/integrable potential for the displayed full-domain functional and first variation.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction gives the same reciprocal formula, explicitly identifies non-integrable singularity on and inside the sphere, and states that the functional is not well defined; its proposed reformulation also withdraws the present obstacle-avoidance claim.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-002 discusses the failure of obstacle avoidance and the singularity/invariance of the potential term, but it does not identify the specific radial differentiation error that makes the displayed source +∇V point inward rather than outward. The force-direction reversal and its sign-specific repair remain unrecognised.

ISSUE-006 identifies that divergence and pressure are not enforced during the time stepping, that a single terminal projection cannot repair the unconstrained trajectory, and that the corrected scheme must project or solve for pressure at every step. This is the same failure described in the gold issue.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The computation uses intermediate velocity fields that violate the incompressibility constraint and only projects at the end, so the resulting trajectory is not an approximation of the constrained evolution.

component_coverage.gold_component: The finite-difference evolution uses non-divergence-free intermediate fields and applies projection only after all updates, so the reported trajectory and final simulation are not established as an incompressible evolution.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction explicitly states that only a terminal projection is performed, that pressure and the divergence constraint are omitted during stepping, and supplies the corresponding per-step projection/pressure repair.
